question: The speed of a train is 90 km/h. What is the distance covered by it in 10 minutes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed** in km/min = 90 ÷ 60 = 1.5 km/min.

**Distance** = 1.5 km/min × 10 min = 15 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed** of the train (S) = 90 km/h

**Time** taken (T) = 10 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Time in hours = Minutes ÷ 60

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ffd035499af9faf2262de6bf44c1679a27d32f69a7b8ed126691617e8e9e8ba2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Convert **time** into hours: T = 10 ÷ 60 = 1/6 hours

⇒ **Distance** = 90 × (1/6)

⇒ **Distance** = 15 km

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. For two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy/(x+y).

Relative Speed

Same direction: Subtract speeds (S₁ − S₂). Opposite direction: Add speeds (S₁ + S₂).</p
